tagline: Piedmont back roads where Greene and Cornwallis ran their race.
intro: The byway sets out from the Guilford-Rockingham county line near Summerfield and wanders more than a hundred miles of back roads and two-lane highways north and east through Caswell County, then down NC 86 through Piedmont dairy country to Hillsborough and Durham.

In early 1781 this was the country of a long chase. Mizpah Church Road, through rolling farmland, hardwood forest and open pasture, loosely follows the colonial Dick's Ferry Road, where Cornwallis hunted for Greene's army as it raced north toward the Dan River, and after Guilford Court House Greene's troops camped at the Troublesome Creek Ironworks. Washington came by on his southern tour of 1791.

moments.title: Yanceyville
moments.text: The Caswell County courthouse, built between 1858 and 1861, mixes the Italian Romanesque with Classical features and is unlike any other courthouse in the state.

moments.title: Milton
moments.text: A river town that grew prosperous on tobacco and corn brought up the Dan by flatboat, and in 1846 turned the railroad away, citing the noise among other concerns.

moments.title: Prospect Hill
moments.text: A red brick building at Prospect Hill and a white brick one at Hightowers, both on NC 86, are general store buildings from the mid-1800s.
